question: What BLEU score did the big Transformer get on English-to-German?
expected_answer: The Transformer (big) achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task [6 Results, p. 8].

question: What BLEU score did the big model get on English-to-French?
expected_answer: The paper reports two numbers: Section 6.1 text states that the big model achieves 41.0 BLEU, while Table 2 lists 41.8 BLEU for the big model on English-to-French [6 Results, p. 8].
ambiguity_notes: Internal paper discrepancy: Section 6.1 text states 41.0, while Table 2 lists 41.8. Both must be reported under Fix 3 rules.

question: What is d_model in the base Transformer?
expected_answer: In the base Transformer model, the embedding and sub-layer output dimension d_model is 512 [3 Model Architecture, p. 3; Table 3, p. 9].

question: How many attention heads are used?
expected_answer: The Multi-Head Attention mechanism in the base Transformer employs h = 8 parallel attention heads [3 Model Architecture, p. 4; Table 3, p. 9].

question: What optimizer and warmup steps are used for training?
expected_answer: The models were trained using the Adam optimizer (beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.98, epsilon = 10^-9) with 4000 warmup steps [5 Training, p. 7].

question: How many GPUs were used for training and which type?
expected_answer: The models were trained on one machine equipped with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs [5 Training, p. 7].

question: How many layers does the encoder have?
expected_answer: The Transformer encoder consists of a stack of N = 6 identical layers [3 Model Architecture, p. 2-3].

question: What accuracy does LeafScan get on the test set?
expected_answer: LeafScan reached 97.8% test accuracy on the PlantLeaf-38 test set [Abstract, p. 1; 5 Results, p. 2, Table 1].

question: What learning rate and batch size were used?
expected_answer: LeafScan was trained with an initial learning rate of 1e-3 (cosine decay down to 1e-5) and a batch size of 64 [4 Experimental Setup, p. 2].

question: How many images are in the dataset and how are they split?
expected_answer: PlantLeaf-38 contains 54,000 leaf images split 70/15/15 into 37,800 training, 8,100 validation, and 8,100 test images [4 Experimental Setup, p. 2].
ambiguity_notes: Scoring rule requires 54,000 and 70. Note that matching 70 alone does not guarantee the full 70/15/15 split is correct, which will be manually inspected.

question: What accuracy does LeafScan get on field photographs?
expected_answer: On real field photographs, LeafScan achieved an accuracy of 81.3% [Abstract, p. 1; 5 Results, p. 3].

question: How many parameters does LeafScan have?
expected_answer: LeafScan has 1.9 million parameters [Abstract, p. 1; 3 Method, p. 1].

question: Which baseline models were compared?
expected_answer: The baseline models compared were MobileNetV2-1.0, EfficientNet-B0, and ResNet-18 [5 Results, p. 2, Table 1].

question: What happens to accuracy when CutMix is removed?
expected_answer: In the ablation study, removing CutMix reduced test accuracy from 97.8% down to 97.1% [5 Results, p. 3, Table 2].

question: What MAPE does GridTCN get?
expected_answer: The paper reports two numbers: Section 5.1 main text states that GridTCN reaches a MAPE of 4.1%, while Table 2 (and Abstract/Conclusion) lists 4.3% [Abstract, p. 1; 5 Results, p. 2, Table 2; 7 Conclusion, p. 3].
ambiguity_notes: Discrepancy: Section 5.1 states 4.1%, Table 2 lists 4.3%. Both numbers must be reported under Fix 3 rules.

question: How many parameters does GridTCN have?
expected_answer: GridTCN has 0.8 million parameters [Abstract, p. 1; 5 Results, p. 2, Table 2; 7 Conclusion, p. 3].

question: What optimiser, learning rate and batch size were used?
expected_answer: GridTCN was trained with the Adam optimizer using a learning rate of 2e-3 and a batch size of 128 [3 Our Approach, p. 2].

question: How many substations are in the dataset and which years does it cover?
expected_answer: The dataset contains hourly demand readings from 120 substations covering January 2021 to December 2023 [4 Data and Evaluation Protocol, p. 2].

question: What MAPE does the LSTM reach when 20% of readings are missing?
expected_answer: When 20% of input values are missing, the LSTM baseline's MAPE rises to 7.3% [Abstract, p. 1; 5 Results, p. 2-3].

question: How long did training take and on what hardware?
expected_answer: GridTCN was trained on an 8-core CPU without GPU in about 3.5 hours [3 Our Approach, p. 2].

question: Which component matters most in the ablation study?
expected_answer: In the ablation study, dilated convolutions matter most; replacing them with standard convolutions degrades MAPE to 5.2% [5 Results, p. 3, Table 3].
